subject: Compliance-first VPC qualification: recap & next actions
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: John Rivera <john.rivera@medbridgehealth.com>, Sarah Tan <sarah.tan@medbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Sep 2027 14:23:00 -0700
Subject: Compliance-first VPC qualification: recap & next actions

Thanks for your time on the call today — quick recap so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps. I captured the pain, success criteria, and the most important constraints we need to validate before an architecture/quote.

Pain & goals (as discussed)
- Customer-managed keys required for all customer data at rest (must be HSM/KMS-backed and accessible under customer control).
- No internet egress from inference nodes; all outbound traffic must go through customer-controlled NAT or a managed proxy.
- Auditability: immutable audit logs for model requests and admin actions, retained for minimum 2 years.
- Low-latency inference for clinical assistant workflows (99th percentile latency SLO target: sub-400ms for median prompt sizes).

Current stack (what John/Sarah described)
- AWS account per environment (prod/preprod) in us-west-2, strict NACLs and private-only subnets.
- Key management: AWS KMS with a customer-managed CMK; they also run an on-prem HSM for vaulting keys for DR.
- Existing bastion and transit VPCs for ops; no public IPs on compute instances.

Success criteria for pilot/POC
- Redwood runs inside customer VPC (private deployment) with zero public egress from worker nodes.
- Integration with customer KMS/HSM for key unwrap/wrap operations or ability to use AWS KMS CMK with customer control.
- Demonstrate audit log delivery to customer SIEM (CloudWatch/Lambda/Direct S3 ingestion) for 14 days of production-like traffic.

Open technical questions (we need answers to proceed)
1) Can you share a minimal network diagram and the allowed inbound/outbound CIDR/IP ranges for the VPC peering/Transit gateway? (attachment: medbridge-network-sketch.png)
2) Will you permit outbound connections to Redwood control-plane endpoints on port 443 for health/status polling, or do you need a fully air-gapped control plane?
3) For KMS/HSM: do you require an HSM appliance in your datacenter for key injection, or is AWS KMS CMK with key policies sufficient?
4) Certificate rotation/OTA: do you have an internal PKI for signing nodes, or should we bring our own signed certs?

Proposed next steps
- Dev workshop: 60–90 minute technical deep-dive to validate network and KMS integration (Dev Patel to lead).
- You to share network diagram + brief compliance contact (name/email) so we can sync on SOC2 artifacts.
- Redwood to produce a short runbook and cost estimate for a single-region pilot (timeline: 2–3 weeks after answers).

Attachments: redwood-private-reqs-checklist.pdf (light checklist), medbridge-network-sketch.png

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Solutions — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0189
From: James O'Neill <james.oneill@mcdermott.com>

Cc: John Rivera <john.rivera@medbridgehealth.com>, Sarah Tan <sarah.tan@medbridgehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Sep 2027 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Compliance-first VPC qualification: recap & next actions

Kimberly — thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick points from MedBridge security (I'm their external compliance consultant):

- On KMS/HSM: medbridge currently requires customer ownership of key material for production PHI workloads; AWS KMS CMK is acceptable only if keys are imported or CMK key policies are tightly controlled. They do have an on-prem HSM (Thales) used for most long-term key custody.
- Air-gap: full air-gap is not required for this POC, but any control-plane telemetry must be able to be routed over a customer-managed proxy; direct outbound to third-party control planes is a hard no for production. POC can use a proxy tunnel.
- Audit logs: SIEM ingestion will be via secure S3 bucket in their account; logs must be delivered in near-real-time (max acceptable lag 5 minutes).

I'll connect you with their security lead (Michael Brown) in the next message — he can provide the specific KMS policy snippets.

—James
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: James O'Neill <james.oneill@mcdermott.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: John Rivera <john.rivera@medbridgehealth.com>, Sarah Tan <sarah.tan@medbridgehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Sep 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Compliance-first VPC qualification: recap & next actions

Appreciate the clarifications, James. Technical notes & asks from our side: 

- KMS/HSM integration options we support today:
  * AWS KMS CMK with key policy and key grants (we can perform envelope encryption and never persist the unwrapped key in plaintext).
  * HSM-backed flow: we can implement a key-wrapping proxy where customer HSM signs/unlocks session keys during startup — requires VPN/peering and an agreed key exchange protocol.
- Control plane connectivity: we can operate with a proxy bastion that tunnels control-plane heartbeats over outbound 443 to a customer-managed proxy. For production, we usually pair that with a signed cert from customer PKI or an mTLS handshake using client certs.
- Audit log delivery: we can push logs to an S3 endpoint in your account with server-side-encryption using your CMK; delivery can be near real-time using a small agent and a buffered uploader.

Action items I need to run the tech workshop and build a pilot plan:
1) Network diagram (including transit gateway, peering, and NAT/proxy details) — John/Sarah to share.
2) KMS policy sample and HSM access model  — Michael (security lead) to share.
3) Access window for the workshop: propose Wed Sep 14 or Thu Sep 15, 10:00–11:30 PT. Please confirm preferred slot.

I'll prepare a short lab plan (30-min hands-on + 45-min Q&A) and a minimal deployment manifest showing S3 log sink, KMS integration points, and egress constraints.

—Dev
